<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `520ea21c16ddaa77b7841261daea1353082a143b` — the merge of head `41b47926643dec979624d5b7a7e6df3d3c5747bf` into base `71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 520ea21c16ddaa77b7841261daea1353082a143b && git checkout 520ea21c16ddaa77b7841261daea1353082a143b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37 41b47926643dec979624d5b7a7e6df3d3c5747bf && git checkout -B drift-repro 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37 && git merge --no-ff 41b47926643dec979624d5b7a7e6df3d3c5747bf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37` → pass the list as

## Contract review

- every consumer of `upsRowsAll` / `upsRows` in `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, with `grantSetNameOf`, `grantOrganizationOf`, `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding`, `mayApply`, the `applyingGrants` loop, and `grant-validity.ts`'s `isGrantActive` and `nextGrantValidityBoundary`;
- `plugin-security`'s `sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`, for its declared columns.

Also the card #24896 with the claim 6295406119 and the dispatch 6295459203, the dev's `os-dev-report` 6296305180 (read as claims), and the PR body.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The projection names every column the resolver reads, and only those: right.**
  - `grantSetNameOf` reads `permission_set`.
  - `grantOrganizationOf` reads `organization_id` (or `organizationId`). Through it, so do `grantAppliesInTenant`, `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding`, `mayApply` and the `applyingGrants` filter.
  - `isGrantActive` and `nextGrantValidityBoundary` read `valid_from` / `valid_until` (or their camelCase spellings).
  - Nothing else reads a grant row. `upsRowsAll` and `upsRows` appear only at the read, the active filter, the `admin_full_access` anchor check, the ledger loop, the `applyingGrants` filter and loop, and the cache boundary. No path reads `id`, `user_id`, `granted_by`, `reason` or `display_title`.
  - All four columns are declared on the object (`permission_set`, `organization_id`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`).
- **The camelCase alternates are not projected: right.** The object declares only the snake_case columns, and the engine keys rows by them, so the alternates never arrive on this read either way. Retiring the helpers' `??` alternates is outside this card; it is noted as an observation and not filed.
- **The read path: right, and nothing else moves.**
  - `tryFind` gains an optional trailing `fields` and passes it through only when given. It is module-private: no export, no public member.
  - The other four prelude reads pass no `fields` and issue the same query as before.
- **The pins have teeth.**
  - **Equivalence** (25 tests): each of twelve grant-state fixtures, plus the 11 batch-equivalence fixtures, resolves the WHOLE envelope twice. Once over full rows with a computed title, once over rows carrying the four named columns and no `id`, as driver-sql answers a projection. The two must be equal.
    - The fixtures cover active, expired, not yet valid, in window, the active organization's, another organization's, deployment-wide (`organization_id` null), and the Default Organization's `admin_full_access` grant acting elsewhere and with no tenant.
    - The dev's column sweep (each column dropped in turn, 11 / 11 / 3 / 6 red) shows that every column is load-bearing.
  - **Count** (in `plugin-auth`): a real engine on SQLite, a direct grant, and the declared title or a one-hop title through `user_id`. The case first asserts the hop is live on an unprojected read (`display_title` resolves the person's name). It then asserts the prelude's exact `PRELUDE_READS` tally and 4 legs.
  - **Ablation:** with the projection reverted, the one-hop count case goes red (`sys_user` 3, expected 2) and the projection case of the equivalence pin goes red. Both legs were restored, blob equal to `HEAD`.
- **The objectql mechanism: as the dev read it.** A `fields` list of stored columns computes no formula and issues no hop (`planFormulaProjection`). #22300's widening applies only to a formula named in the list. The count pin measures it on the real engine.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for `@objectstack/core`: right. Every resolved authz answer is unchanged and pinned so; no accept set, served shape, export or error code moves.
- `Clause-②: no (…)` is at a line start in the changeset (line 7) and in the PR body.
- `check-governed-merges` matched 0 of 4 paths; 309 changed lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1** (the `plugin-auth` pin, cross-lane): accepted. The claim named it, it is the card's own "Done when", and it is test-only. The seat declared it on `domain:services`' seat post #6021 at 6296470031.
- **Deviation 2** (the equivalence pin on the recording double): accepted. `core` cannot import `objectql`. The double answers a projection as driver-sql does, and the real-engine leg is the count pin.
- **Deviation 3** (the model-free trailer pair): accepted; that is AGENTS.md's form.
- **Deviation 4** (the dev did not subscribe to the PR): accepted; the seat holds the subscription.
- **Deviation 5** (#22300 read through its landed mechanism; the #24775 / #24523 / #24515 threads not opened): accepted. The card carried the measurements.
- **Deviation 6** (shallow-clone note; `check-plugin-teardown-shape` and its self-test ran, exit 0): accepted.
- **Deviation 7** (three pushes to the one branch): accepted.
- **Open questions:** all three taken as the dev settled them: a positional optional `fields`, snake_case only, and the double plus the real-engine count pin.
- **Out-of-scope findings:** `sys_member` and `sys_user_position` are unprojected too, but their titles read only own columns, so they cost no read today. The camelCase alternates are a dormant tolerance with no producer. Neither meets a filing gate.
- **The merge:** `git merge-tree` against today's `origin/main` is clean.
- **Check-runs on `41b4792664`:** not concluded at this read (`ci-failure` UNDETERMINED, 7 still running). The ACCEPT waits for green.
